title: Microsoft Purview DLP: adaptive scopes for SharePoint sites
summary: Hold: the briefing presents an incompletely documented PowerShell parameter as a working scoping command and carries daily evaluation behaviour from retention and auto-labeling into DLP without confirmation. The static policy creation path also omits a required template selection. The roadmap facts and general DLP licensing are supported.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "<policy name>" -SharePointAdaptiveScopes <values> is documented as the operation that attaches SharePoint adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePointAdaptiveScopes scope values New-DlpCompliancePolicy; opened its reference. Syntax lists the parameter, but its description is '{{ Fill SharePointAdaptiveScopes Description }}'; no passage explains what values identify a scope or what the parameter does.

Replace 'Attach the scope to a new test DLP policy' with 'Confirm Microsoft's documented method for attaching the scope before testing a new DLP policy.'

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope's reference describes adaptive scopes as used in retention policies and retention label policies.
claims.quote: Use the New-AdaptiveScope cmdlet to create adaptive scopes in your organization. Adaptive scopes (or static scopes) are used in retention policies and retention label policies.

claims.where: controls[2].ui
claims.claim: The static DLP wizard path needs only one Custom selection between Enterprise applications & devices and Assign admin units.
claims.quote: Select Enterprise applications & devices. Select Custom from both the Categories list and the Regulations list. ... Accept the default Full directory on the Assign admin units page.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].ui.path with 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose where to apply the policy > SharePoint sites'. The cited procedure requires both Custom choices.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The general adaptive scopes page's daily query schedule applies to SharePoint DLP and can be used when allowing for coverage changes.

claims.fix: Replace the Autonomy & actions timing sentence with 'The roadmap describes automatic membership changes; Microsoft's DLP evaluation interval is not yet documented.' Remove 'allowing for the daily query run Learn describes' from After rollout and remove daily timing as a verified DLP premise from the risk rationale. Keep the explicitly attributed background comparison and open question.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk

In Data exposure, replace the validation premise with 'The general adaptive scopes page warns that typed values are not immediately validated, but it does not state whether DLP uses this configuration.' Remove unvalidated values as a confirmed DLP premise from the risk rationale.
